..
Issued at 1224 AM CST Sat Nov 7 2026

An upper-level trough is digging into the Four Corners region with a 
subtropical jet streak forecast to move over South Texas. This, 
combined with a 500 hPa closed low cutting off from the main flow 
and residing over northern Mexico by Sunday. Closer to the surface, 
easterly flow will result in upslope flow against the Sierra Madre 
Oriental ranges in northeastern Mexico. Latest REFS and Canadian 
guidance shows that this orographically induced vertical ascent will 
start off this rain event for locations along the Rio Grande and 
into the Edwards Plateau Saturday afternoon and evening. Early 
Sunday morning, the LLJ and approaching frontal system further 
enhances the shower/storm activity across the Brush Country. 
Forecast soundings across the Brush Country shows skinny CAPE 
profiles with the warm cloud layer pushing 10k ft and PWATS climbing 
to near 2.0" (approaching the +2SD), effective warm rain processes 
and convectively enhanced rainfall rates are looking to be in store 
across South Texas throughout Sunday and spreading towards the 
coastline. The limiting factors that may keep rainfall totals will 
be the positioning of the surface front (does it make it down into 
Deep South Texas, or stay closer to the region between Corpus 
Christi and Baffin Bays. The convergence along this line will be 
the secondary area of the highest rainfall totals. Should this front 
make it into Deep South Texas, the convectively induced higher 
rainfall rates may remain south of the Benavides area. Either way, 
given the increased confidence in multiple areas of higher rainfall 
rates/totals and overall guidance painting 2-4 inches through Monday 
morning with localized 5+" totals (and yes, some guidance has gone 
as high as 9 inches, though this is on the extreme end), a Flood 
Watch has been issued for most of South Texas from this afternoon 
through Monday morning. While flash flood guidance is on the higher 
end (generally 3 to 5 inches for a 6 hr period), should any of these 
storms start training or slow-moving over the same areas (and 
especially over the urban areas of Laredo and along the Coastal 
Bend), flash flooding may become a concern. For this reason, the WPC 
has included most areas under a Marginal Risk for Excessive Rainfall 
(level 1 of 4), and a Slight Risk (level 2 of 4) on Sunday across 
South Texas. 

Temperatures today will be near seasonal for most locations (upper 
70s/low 80s) with lows in the 60s/70s for Sunday morning. Temps on 
Sunday will struggle to climb much more from the morning low and 
temperatures dropping into the 50s across the northern Brush Country 
by Monday morning. This isentropically induced rainfall event will 
start winding down throughout the day on Monday. Low-end rainfall 
chances (10-30%) will continue through Wednesday (better chances 
closer to the coast). Then higher pressure builds in as an 
additional mid-level trough moves through the South Central Plains. 
This northerly flow will usher in drier air (PWATs dropping from 
1.5" values on Wednesday down to 0.75" PWATs by Friday). This will 
keep highs slightly below normal and the return of widespread 50s 
for low temperatures by the start of the upcoming weekend.

Outside of the threat of heavy rainfall this weekend, there are also 
concerns for coastal flooding as the new moon phase approaches this 
weekend, combined with 20-25 kt E/NE'ly winds. While the wave energy 
is currently forecast to not exceed 7-8 seconds, P-ETSS guidance 
along the Middle Texas Coast is forecasting water levels reaching 2-
2.5 ft for the high tide cycles from Sunday through at least mid-
week. This will make for tricky driving conditions on local beaches 
(combined with the downpours) and for those parking along our local 
bays and estuaries could see periods where water levels will make 
certain areas impassable. Small Craft Advisory conditions will also 
be needed for the open Gulf waters from mid-morning Sunday through 
Monday morning. Lastly, these strong easterlies will lead to a High 
Rip Current Risk Sunday into Sunday night.
